3  COMMON ORDER

Counsel for the petitioners has filed a memo for withdrawal of the petition as against petitioner No.1 - accused No.2.
2.

The contents of the memo are as under:
"That the advocate for the petitioner beg to submit memo as under.
That the petitioner No.1 in the above petition is not pressing the above petition.
Hence the Hon'ble Court be pleased permit the petitioner No.1 to withdraw the above petition with a liberty to file discharge application before Trial Court to meet ends of justice."
3. Heard.
Perused the petition and memo.

The Criminal Petition No.101851/2023 is filed by accused No.1 and Criminal Petition No.100194/2023 is filed by accused Nos.2 to 4 under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. to quash the complaint dated 26.07.2022 registered in Crime No.56/2022 dated 26.07.2022 of Women Police Station, Dharwad, charge sheet dated 07.10.2022, order of taking cognizance dated 11.10.2022 in C.C. No.1393/2022 on the file of II Addl. Civil Judge and JMFC- NC: 2024:KHC-D:7756 II, Dharwad for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 read with Section 34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of DP Act.

4. The brief facts of the de-facto complainant are as under:
On 26.07.2022, the de-facto complainant / party in person lodged complaint,
alleging that her marriage solemnized with accused No.1 on 28.12.2020 (registered on 28.12.2020) and on 29.12.2021 said marriage was arranged by both the family at Kanakabhavan Kalyan Mantap, Karatagi.
At the time of marriage, 7 tholas of gold jewelleries, 1 k.g. silver articles and other marriage related articles were given to accused No.1 and incurred marriage expenses of Rs.5,00,000/-.

After the marriage,
the relationship of de-facto complainant and accused No.1 was cordial.

Accused No.1 and de-facto complainant started their marital life at Karatagi, accused No.3 - Sandeep - brother-in-law, accused No.4 - Asha - sister-in-law of de-facto complainant used to visit matrimonial house once in 15 days.
At that time, accused Nos.1 to 4 demanded the de-facto complainant to bring additional dowry and also intentionally NC: 2024:KHC-D:7756 insulted her in filthy language.
Thereby they harassed the de- facto complainant physically and mentally.
On 18.03.2022, the de-facto complainant and accused No.1 went to Karatagi to perform jatra mahotsav.
At that time, accused Jayaprakash S/O. Virupakshappa ...

vs The State Of Karnataka on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190277349/
4 No.1 assaulted her and family caused hurt infront of Venkateshwara temple,
Karatagi.
On 20.03.2022 in the morning, her husband and her mother-in-law took quarrel with de-facto complainant, assaulted her and caused bodily injury.
In this regard, she approached Karatagi Police to take action.
In turn, the Karatagi Police secured bond from accused No.1, wherein, he undertaken to take care of the de-facto complainant for a period of six months.
Again the accused persons harassed her.
Hence, she lodged complaint on 26.07.2022.
Taking exception to the same, accused No.1 filed Criminal Petition No.101851/2023 and accused Nos.2 to 4 filed Criminal Petition No.100194/2023, to quash the entire proceedings.

5. The counsel for petitioners submitted that as per the allegations made in complaint, FIR and column No.17 of charge sheet, there is prima facie allegation against accused No.1 and there are no specific allegation against accused Nos.2 to 4.
It is contended that the de-facto complainant herself NC: 2024:KHC-D:7756 shows certain dates of cause of action.

On those dates, she made allegations against accused No.1 that, on 18.03.2022, accused No.1 assaulted the de-facto complainant and on 20.03.2022, accused Nos.1 and 2 caused injury on the person of de-facto complainant.

Except these allegations, there are general and omnibus allegations against accused Nos.3 and 4 and hence, the ingredients of Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 read with Section 34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of D.P.
Act are not attracted.
Thus, the counsel prayed to allow the petitions.
6. Learned HCGP for respondent No.1 and learned counsel party-in-person vehemently argued and submitted that there are prima facie allegations against accused Nos.1 to 4.

Accused Nos.1 to 4 harassed the de-facto complainant physically and mentally in order to bring more dowry from her parental house and in this regard, they assaulted, abused her and made criminal intimidation to de-facto complainant.
There is prima facie allegation against accused Nos.1 to 4.
Thus, prayed to dismiss the petitions.
Perused the order sheet maintained by the Trial Court in C.C. No.1393/2022.
The learned Magistrate after accepting the charge sheet took cognizance of the aforesaid offences and issued summons.
Taking exception of the same, these petitioners have filed these petitions for quashment.
8. Perused the complaint, FIR and column No.17 of charge sheet.
The de-facto complainant has specifically stated that she was thrown out from the matrimonial house in the month of July 2022.
On 18.03.2022 accused No.1 assaulted her and on 20.03.2022 accused Nos.1 and 2 assaulted her and voluntarily caused hurt in respect of demand of dowry.
They abused her in filthy language.
The incident took place on 18.03.2022 and 20.03.2022 and the complaint was lodged on 26.07.2022.
From the perusal of the material available on record, there is prima facie allegation against accused Nos.1 and 2 only.

Further, there are some omnibus and general allegations against accused Nos.3 and 4 and there is no specific allegation made against accused Nos.3 and 4 as to how and in what manner they subjected the de-facto complainant to cruelty, both mentally and physically and also demanded to bring money from her parental house.

sentences.text: In this case, there is delay of four months in lodging complaint, but, the de-facto complainant has not offered any plausible explanation.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of State of Andhra Pradesh vs. M.Madhusudhan Rao1 2008 15 SCC 581 at para 30 has held as follows:
"30.

entities.text: State of Andhra Pradesh vs. M.Madhusudhan Rao1 2008 15 SCC 581
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Time and again, the object and importance of prompt lodging of the First Information Report has been highlighted.
Delay in lodging the First Information Report, more often than not, results in embellishment and exaggeration, which is a creature of an afterthought.

A delayed report not only gets bereft of the advantage of spontaneity, the danger of the introduction of coloured version, exaggerated account of the incident or a concocted story as a result of deliberations and consultations, also creeps in, casting a serious doubt on its veracity.

Therefore, it is essential that the delay in lodging the report should be satisfactorily explained."
(2008) 15 SCC 582 - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:7756 10.

Further, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Kahkashan Kausar alias Sonam and others vs.
State of Bihar2 at para 18 has held as follows:
"18.

State of Bihar2

sentences.text: Coming to the facts of this case, upon a perusal of the contents of the FIR dated 01.04.19, it is revealed that general allegations are levelled against the Appellants.
The complainant alleged that 'all accused harassed her mentally and threatened her of terminating her pregnancy'.

Furthermore, no specific and distinct allegations have been made against either of the Appellants herein, i.e., none of the Appellants have been attributed any specific role in furtherance of the general allegations made against them.
This simply leads to a situation wherein one fails to ascertain the role played by each accused in furtherance of the offence.

The allegations are, therefore,
general and omnibus and can at best be said to have been made out on account of small skirmishes.
Insofar as husband is concerned, since he has not appealed against the order of the High Court, we have not examined the veracity of allegations made against him.
However, as far as the Appellants are concerned, the allegations made against them being general and omnibus, do not warrant prosecution."

The cognizance taken by the learned Magistrate for the aforesaid offences is without any substance.
Even otherwise, the last event that has taken place on 20.03.2022 and the FIR was lodged on 26.07.2022 without offering any plausible explanation.
12. In view of the preceding analysis, the continuation of criminal proceedings as against accused Nos.2 and 3 - accused Nos.3 and 4 will be an abuse of process of law.
However, there is prima facie material against accused Nos.1 and 2.

(i) Criminal Petition No.101851/2023 filed by the petitioner - accused No.1
is dismissed.

(ii) Criminal Petition No.100194/2023 is allowed (accused Nos.3 and 4).
